summary: Read-only review; nothing was built or executed, and no shell/git tool was available, so the 13-file delta was reconstructed by reading the changed files, the agent status record, and the pinned Basalt 4c5c9e9 / vendored UCAN / replay-ledger code they call. Abbreviations: WT = /home/brittonr/.cargo-target/agents-20261030/attenuation/worktree ; BAS = /home/brittonr/.cargo/git/checkouts/basalt-d217f0a83bebd193/4c5c9e9. Reviewed: WT/src/remote_build/attenuated_admission.rs, authority_caveats.rs, WT/src/remote_build.rs (TicketAuthRequest, RemoteProductionServerContext, commit_remote_ticket_admission_for_state, serve/start wiring, ticket-create report), WT/src/nix_gateway/authority.rs (+authority/tests.rs), WT/crates/crunch-store/src/restricted_view.rs (+lib.rs), WT/src/store_cmd.rs, WT/src/remote_build/tests/{attenuated_admission,endpoint_binding}_tests.rs, WT/tests/remote_credentials_cli.rs, WT/docs/remote-credentials.md, design.md/specs/tasks.md, ADR 0090, the status record, plus crunch-nix-gateway/src/replay.rs, remote_credential_state.rs, endpoint*.rs, caveat.rs call sites, BAS mantle.rs / ucan_enforcement/shell.rs and vendored UCAN holder_invocation.rs / durable_authority.rs / token.rs / verified.rs. Result: on the production local-build receiver the new path is mechanically sound and fail-closed. The grant check runs inside the ticket-state flock after bearer and request validation and before redemption (remote_build.rs:13545-13561); every denial collapses to one constant string and no frame is written (13293-13297); the receiver's own clock, endpoint, project scope, revocation, trusted roots, proofs, keys and replay ledger are used; caveat decoding is strict, bounded and has no panic sites; the restricted store lookup gates before every read. No exploitable fail-open or reason/job/path oracle was found in the new code. The substantive problems concern what the control delivers: F1 (high) the presentation is optional and the bearer alone admits, so any delegatee can drop the restriction - exactly the weakness ADR 0090 rejects - and the status record does not say so; F2 'job' is a sender-chosen label, so a granted label admits arbitrary payloads and job ids; F3 the shared 8,192-record replay ledger has no GC and fails closed silently; F4 holder attenuation needs operator provisioning of proofs and keys. Several claims overstate (digest covers 'the whole request'; 'an invalid snapshot stops remote serve'; T3.2/T3.4 'delivered' although the store view has no production producer and gateway/project chain reports have no production caller). Tests exercise the real admission function for most negatives but never inspect the replay ledger, the CLI/process boundary, or a serve-path admit. Recommendation: merge as non-accepted groundwork (statuses stay 'implemented, not accepted'; T3.1-T3.4 stay unticked) and track the follow-ups below.

findings.title: Remote attenuation is advisory: the presentation is optional and the bearer alone admits, so any delegatee can drop the restriction (the weakness ADR 0090 rejects)
findings.evidence: remote_build.rs:13588-13590: `let Some(presentation) = auth.attenuated_grant.as_ref() else { return Ok(()); };` - no presentation means unchanged legacy admission. The bearer is the only mandatory credential (verify_credentials at 13545-13557 runs before the grant check at 13559) and RemoteTicket (remote_credentials.rs:447-457, deny_unknown_fields) has no 'requires grant' property. design.md:71-72: 'Legacy ticket admission remains unchanged when no attenuated grant is presented.' ADR 0090:9: 'Possession of an unrestricted parent bearer cannot be made into a non-bypassable holder-attenuated child merely by appending an unsigned restriction: the holder can pass the original bearer instead.' docs/remote-credentials.md:143 does admit 'a holder who also holds the ticket bearer can omit the presentation and use the ticket unrestricted', but the status record row for T3.1 (line 18) says 'Delivered' and never mentions the bypass.
findings.scenario: An operator issues ticket T (up to 100,000 uses) and an issuer delegates a UCAN restricted to /job/r1/output/action. Admission always requires the bearer, so every recipient that can be admitted at all holds T. The recipient sends AuthTicket without `attenuated_grant`; the early return at 13590 skips every caveat check and the receiver redeems T for any job within the ticket limits. The restriction binds only parties who volunteer to attach it (self-restriction/audit). The spec scenario 'Restricted grant refuses a second job' holds only for requests that carry the presentation. docs:143 also implies a class of bearer-less holders who are bound; no admission path exists for them.
findings.recommendation: Before ticking T3.1 or accepting ADR 0090 add an enforcing mode: a per-ticket 'attenuation required' property persisted in ticket state (schema bump) or, minimally, 'when attenuation-authority.json is provisioned every admission on this endpoint must carry a valid presentation'; and/or a bearer-less grant admission path whose use accounting is keyed to the holder. Until then state the limit prominently in the status record, ADR consequences and docs, and reword docs:137/143.

findings.title: Job identity is a sender-chosen label: caveats see only request_id and payload kind, not the production job_id, declared output names or payload content
findings.evidence: attenuated_admission.rs:125: `let target = format!('/job/{}/output/{}', request.request_id, output_class(request));` with output_class returning only 'derivation' or 'action' (90-96). `job_id` (line 131, from request.production_attempt) and expected output names (153-155) are only hashed into the holder-signed digest, never into the caveat-visible value. design.md:64-67 requires the declared job identity to include 'production_attempt.job_id' when an attempt exists and the output class to be 'the validated payload kind and declared output names'. production_attempt is mandatory at the production receiver (serve_stdio_remote_production_once_with_commit, remote_build.rs:13255-13293, 'remote-production-attempt-missing').
findings.scenario: A grant for /job/r1/output/action admits any action payload (any spec_json command), any expected output names, any production_attempt.job_id/attempt_id, and any number of submissions (each with a fresh holder nonce) as long as request_id is 'r1'. A holder can run unrelated work, or work attributed to another coordinator job id, under the granted label; only a different label is refused, so 'one declared job' really means one label.
findings.recommendation: Put job_id and declared output names into the filter target, or require exact-resource grants whose issuer-signed capability includes the request digest, and document that prefix-resource grants are label-scoped.

findings.title: Replay ledger is capped at 8,192 records with no expiry/GC, shared by all holders; exhaustion silently and permanently disables every attenuated admission, and the nonce is burned before redemption
findings.evidence: replay.rs:41 `const MAX_RECORDS: usize = 8_192;`; :216-218 `if previous.is_none() && state.records.len() >= MAX_RECORDS { return Err(invalid_state()); }`; :275 validate_state rejects more records; the file has no remove/retain/prune. The error becomes HolderInvocationReplayError::Backend (BAS vendor/ucan/src/durable_authority.rs admit_parts) -> Denied -> the constant string, with no local log (remote_build.rs:13591-13594). Every admitted presentation takes one slot permanently and does so before redemption (attenuated_admission.rs:207-215 precedes remote_build.rs:13561). TICKET_USES_MAX = 100_000 (remote_credentials.rs:22). replay.rs:171-172: rename then directory fsync; a failure of the fsync reports an error although the record is already in place.
findings.scenario: A holder with a valid bearer and a valid grant signs 8,192 distinct nonces and opens 8,192 admissions (abandoning each after AuthOk), or a busy CI simply reaches the cap. From then on every attenuated presentation by every holder on that receiver is denied with remote-attenuated-grant-denied and no local diagnostic. Recovery needs a new ledger directory, which also resets nonce history unless the authority generation is bumped and grants re-issued; docs:141 does not describe this. The same slot is burned when effective_caveat_chain (attenuated_admission.rs:217) or ticket persistence (remote_build.rs:13561-13570, 'remote-ticket-state-commit-failed') fails after verify.
findings.recommendation: Prune records by token expiry, add per-tenant quotas, emit a distinct local error/log for ledger-full and backend failures, and document ledger rotation together with generation bump and grant re-issue.

findings.title: Holder attenuation is operator-gated: parent proofs and every delegate/holder key must be pre-provisioned in the receiver snapshot; the presentation carries no proofs
findings.evidence: authority.rs:198-217 builds `keys: ucan::KeyResolutionContext::new(keys)` and `proofs: ucan::ProofCollection::from_tokens(proofs)` only from the snapshot (limits 256 keys, 256 proofs, 8192 revoked, 1 MiB file, authority.rs:181-183 and MAX_AUTHORITY_BYTES). AttenuatedGrantPresentation has no proof field. The test fixture's sign() pushes each parent proof into the snapshot and publish() writes a new revision for every grant (tests:119-124, 143-207).
findings.scenario: H2 wants to sub-delegate to H3 with one extra reject. H3's token references H2's token by hash and is signed by H3's issuer key; the receiver can resolve neither unless the operator republishes attenuation-authority.json. The ADR decision driver 'A holder must be able to delegate less authority without consulting the issuer' is therefore not met at this receiver, and the snapshot becomes a registry of every grant (a 257th proof makes every presentation fail closed).
findings.recommendation: Document the requirement; if unilateral sub-delegation is intended, carry bounded proofs/keys in the presentation under operator-trusted roots.

findings.title: Documentation and doc-comment claim the digest covers the whole request; eight request fields are unbound
findings.evidence: Doc comment: 'a digest over the whole validated request so no other field can change after signing'; docs:139: 'changing any field after signing fails' and lists 'job and attempt identity'. The digest (129-156) covers endpoint_id, store_prefix, request_id, production_attempt.job_id, target, payload id, blake3(payload body), input_refs, source_input_refs, upload_bytes, build_time_limit_secs, expected_outputs (name, logical_path). It does not cover contains_raw_frontend_eval, production_attempt.attempt_id and fence_generation, transfer_policy, resource_requirements, locality_scope, failure_debug_policy, failure_replay, or the endpoint_binding fields other than the name. The only 'changed field' test mutates build_time_limit_secs (tests:457-458). The presentation is also not bound to a ticket id.
findings.scenario: A coordinator or relay between holder and receiver can alter attempt/fence identity, transfer policy, resource requirements, failure-debug policy or locality scope after signing without invalidating the presentation, contrary to the documented tamper-evidence; the same presentation can also be used with any ticket the sender holds. Impact is low because no caveat constrains these fields and the holder chooses them anyway, but the stated guarantee is false.
findings.recommendation: Either extend the digest (attempt_id, fence_generation, transfer_policy, resource_requirements, failure_debug_policy, locality_scope, failure_replay, ticket id) or reword the comment, docs and status record to list exactly what is bound.

findings.title: remote serve does not fail at start on a content-invalid snapshot, contrary to the doc comment and docs
findings.evidence: Doc comment: 'A provisioned but unreadable, non-private or malformed snapshot fails the server start closed'; docs:141: 'a present but invalid snapshot stops remote serve before it reads a request'. GatewayVerifier::open (authority.rs:160-168) only runs `let _ = private_read(...)?` (open with O_NOFOLLOW, regular file, owner, mode, size) and PrivateReplayLedger::new (private directory); it never parses the JSON or checks version, validity window, policy hash, keys, roots or proofs - that happens per request in load() (170-191). No test provisions an invalid snapshot at start (tests:92-117 only loads a valid one).
findings.scenario: An operator ships a truncated or expired attenuation-authority.json (or one whose policy hash is wrong): remote serve starts normally, bearer-only traffic works, and every presented grant is denied with the constant string and no local log, so the misconfiguration surfaces only as unexplained client failures. Fail-closed per request, not fail-open.
findings.recommendation: Call load(now) (parse + window + policy + proofs + keys) from open_operator_authority at start, add negative start tests (malformed, expired, wrong policy hash, non-0600, symlink, oversized), or correct the docs.

findings.title: A presented grant is silently ignored by non-enforcing admission paths; --executor defaults to the fixture path
findings.evidence: main.rs:2801 `#[arg(long, value_enum, default_value = 'fixture')] executor`. serve_stdio_remote_fixture_once and admit_remote_builder_frames_with_auth_facts (remote_build.rs:10562-10591) and the loopback path (12032-12045) call redeem_after_queue without ever reading `auth.attenuated_grant`; only commit_remote_ticket_admission_for_state consults it (13559). open_operator_authority still runs for the fixture executor (14236) but the verifier is unused there. TicketAuthRequest has no deny_unknown_fields (349-350) and the server advertises no attenuation capability, so an older receiver also drops the field.
findings.scenario: An operator who omits --executor local-build, or a client talking to an older receiver, sends a restricted grant; the ticket is redeemed and the request answered with no enforcement and no error, while the same presentation would be refused on the local-build path.
findings.recommendation: Deny (constant string) a presented grant on every non-enforcing path, advertise an attenuation capability in the hello so clients can refuse non-enforcing receivers, and do not default --executor to a path that skips enforcement.

findings.title: Restricted store view has no production producer; Info opens the store before the gate; admitted PathInfo discloses out-of-view references
findings.evidence: store_cmd.rs:138 hard-codes `view: None` in the only production caller (cmd_store); the only LogicalPathView implementations are test-local (ExactSet in restricted_view.rs tests, ExactPaths at store_cmd.rs:2668); no adapter from FilterChain/UCAN to a view exists and admit_exact_store_path in crunch-remote-core is unused, so 'a declared logical-path pattern' (tasks T3.2) is not delivered - only exact path sets. In the Info arm `open_store(context).await?` (store_cmd.rs:187) runs before restricted_info_entries (788) gates the path. cmd_store_info (776-960) prints references, deriver, signatures and node of the admitted path unredacted in restricted mode.
findings.scenario: No CLI or grant can currently turn the restriction on, so the control is inert in production. If a producer is added, a denied (out-of-view) `store info` still opens the backend (with whatever startup effects that has) and an admitted in-view path discloses the names of out-of-view store paths through its references/deriver.
findings.recommendation: Add the production adapter (FilterChain/UCAN session -> LogicalPathView) and CLI input before claiming T3.2; parse and gate the path before open_store; decide whether references/deriver may be shown under a view.

findings.title: No local diagnostics on denial (contrary to the design) and the audit line is logged before redemption commits
findings.evidence: `.map_err(|_| denied())` (13594) discards the cause and the Denied type carries none; the only tracing call is the success line `tracing::info!(target: 'mantle::remote::attenuation', effective_caveat_chain = %report, 'attenuated grant admitted')` at 13597, emitted before redeem_and_commit_ticket_state (13561) can fail with 'remote-ticket-state-commit-failed'. Design: 'Debugging aid stays in local logs.'
findings.scenario: Ledger exhaustion, a corrupt ledger, an expired/invalid snapshot or a wrong endpoint binding all look identical (constant denial, nothing in logs). Conversely the audit log can say 'admitted' for a request whose ticket use was never redeemed.
findings.recommendation: Log a local, reason-coded denial at warn/debug (never to the sender) from a richer internal error type, and move the admission log after the redemption commit.

findings.title: UCAN verification, snapshot parsing and an fsync'd ledger rewrite now run under the global ticket-state lock
findings.evidence: The guard taken at 13526 is held through admit_attenuated_presentation_before_redemption (13559). Inside, load() re-reads and parses up to 1 MiB and the policy (authority.rs:170-217), the token chain is verified several times (authority.rs:281, BAS mantle.rs:228-265, shell.rs prepare_prospective_authority, holder_invocation.rs:768), the ledger takes shared then exclusive flocks (5 s each) and rewrites the whole state with two fsyncs (replay.rs:138-176). Waiting admissions time out after 5 s (remote_credential_state.rs:29,87-95). endpoint.rs:1-7 states 'Ticket mutation locks remain independent and short.'
findings.scenario: Any holder with a valid bearer can lengthen the critical section per request; a slow ledger lock or disk makes other admissions fail with lock-timeout.
findings.recommendation: Measure and bound the critical section, or verify the UCAN chain before taking the ticket lock and take only the replay CAS inside it.

findings.title: Test gaps and a tautological assertion limit what the remote fixtures prove
findings.evidence: assert_refused_without_effect takes `before = self.state()` at line 289 AFTER the caller already ran the admission (call sites 342 and 460-461 evaluate the argument first), so `assert_eq!(self.state(), before)` at 291 is a tautology for the 11 loop cases; only `uses_remaining == TICKET_USES` (292) is meaningful (it is the only field redemption mutates), yet the status record says 'state byte-equal'. No test snapshots or compares the replay ledger directory. The serve-path negative (535-587) exercises one reason (unknown caveat, line 552) and there is no serve-path positive. Not exercised at the receiver: not-yet-valid token, wrong endpoint, generation, audience, holder key or signature, drop/modify/duplicate/reorder of a parent caveat, revoked parent proof, unregistered caveat domain/type, concurrent presentations, ledger-full or write failure, invalid/expired snapshot at start, fixture-path behaviour.
findings.scenario: A regression that consumed the replay nonce before the caveat check, or that wrongly admitted a not-yet-valid or wrong-endpoint grant, would pass this suite.
findings.recommendation: Capture `before` ahead of the call, snapshot the ledger directory, add the missing negatives plus a serve-path admit, and correct the status wording.

findings.title: Project site and chain report: nested goals admitted, no production caller, report overclaims
findings.evidence: authority.rs:137-143 project_value: `suffix.split('/').all(project_segment)` admits goal/packages/check (the test fixture template is /project/project-a/goal/packages/check, authority/tests.rs ~520) while design.md:123-124 says 'nested goal rejected'; resolve_project_target_with_authority has no production caller (only tests; module carries #![allow(dead_code)] at project_build/authority.rs:3 and verify_project_declaration is #[allow(dead_code)] at authority.rs:241). effective_caveat_chain (authority.rs:358-372) is called only by remote admission and a unit test, checks expiry but not revocation, and from_documents labels a zero-caveat chain 'holder-attenuated-ucan' with status 'no-caveats' (authority_caveats.rs:219-225). The ticket-create report prints a constant legacy chain (remote_build.rs:14554).
findings.scenario: Nested goals cannot leave /project/<owner>/ (owner prefix enforced on original and every output, authority.rs:299-303, 130-135), so the risk is latent; the design text, not the code, conflicts with real selectors (ProjectTarget::Attribute is a segment list). The report adds no authorization dependency, but T3.4 'delivered for verified gateway/project sessions' overstates: no production code emits it, and a zero-caveat UCAN is described as 'holder-attenuated'.
findings.recommendation: Correct the design to 'normalized segments in the owner namespace' or enforce an explicit depth bound; wire or drop the gateway/project report; label zero-caveat chains as unrestricted.

findings.title: Snapshot rollback guard is per process, but remote serve is stdio-once; revocation freshness equals file contents
findings.evidence: `observed: Mutex<(u64,[u8;32])>` is initialised to (0,[0;32]) in open() (166) and updated in load() (211); every remote serve process builds a fresh verifier, so the 'same-revision rollback or replacement' protection (comment at 154-156) never triggers across requests. Revocations are admitted with observed_at/effective_from = issued_unix_s and expires_at = expires_unix_s (authority.rs ~433-455), i.e. current for the whole snapshot window.
findings.scenario: Restoring an older backup of attenuation-authority.json (fewer revocations) is accepted by the next process; a grant revoked after the last publish stays valid until the operator publishes. Requires operator-level write access, so informational.
findings.recommendation: Document that revocation freshness is the snapshot window; keep issued/expires tight and persist the high-water revision beside the ledger.

invariants.name: I1 An unknown caveat denies everything
invariants.evidence: authority_caveats.rs:48-51 policy_for returns Some only for (mantle, filter-v1), so any other identity reaches UCAN's CaveatPolicyMissing denial (BAS vendor/ucan/src/token.rs:2642-2651); with_decoded_chain returns None for another domain/type, empty or >8192-byte payload, unparsable JSON, duplicate/unknown JSON fields (authority_caveats.rs:81-104); an unknown kind inside filter-v1 becomes Filter::DenyAll (caveat.rs:226). Exercised at the receiver by the 'unknown-caveat' loop case and the serve-path test (tests:422,552). Unregistered domain/type is not exercised at the receiver.

invariants.name: I2 Caveats compose right-to-left and a longer chain can never widen a grant
invariants.evidence: apply_prefix iterates newest-first (caveat.rs:325-330); from_records enforces length <= 8 and exact ordinals 00..07 in list order (caveat.rs:290-310); with_decoded_chain bounds the chain first (authority_caveats.rs:82-84). UCAN's own preservation is set containment of (domain,type,key,payload) and allows extras in any position (BAS vendor/ucan/src/verified.rs:1058-1070,2443-2461; token.rs:3351-3357,3472-3478), so ordering and gap/duplicate defence rests entirely on Mantle's ordinal check. Receiver tests cover ordinal-gap, over-bound and at-bound; UCAN-level drop/modify/duplicate/reorder of a parent caveat is not exercised at the receiving boundary.

invariants.name: I3 A new rewrite is re-evaluated against every ancestor prefix on the original input, including each output's site policy
invariants.evidence: admit_with_policy (caveat.rs:338-355) checks the site policy on the original and, for every prefix end in 1..=len, on apply_prefix(original,end); PatternPolicies::evaluate requires intersect(...) == expected (authority_caveats.rs:53-66); remote site policy is `value == exact` (authority.rs:299-303). Receiver fixture 'parent-rejected-input-rewritten' (tests:396-463) refuses the laundering chain without redemption.

invariants.name: I4 Receiver uses its own clock, revocation, replay and site-policy facts
invariants.evidence: Clock: ProductionClockPort -> unix_time_now_s (remote_build.rs:13479-13487, host_environment.rs:99-118) read once under the lock (13539) and passed to bearer and grant (13545, 13559; attenuated_admission.rs:207-215); sender now_unix_s/client_endpoint are ignored (remote_build.rs:352-356; test tests:493-516 passes u64::MAX). Endpoint id and project scope come from the operator EndpointBinding (remote_build.rs:13421-13425; endpoint_config.rs:114-130). Revocations, trusted roots, keys, proofs, policy come from the operator snapshot re-read per call (authority.rs:170-217, Loaded::revocations). Site policy is derived from the validated request (bind_remote_job:125; authority.rs:297-303). Strict zero-skew UCAN limits (authority.rs:287,480; token.rs:1664-1673), half-open expiry (authority.rs:177-178,292), saturating arithmetic in UCAN (verified-logic ucan_token.rs:69-80); no arithmetic in the new Mantle code. Sender-supplied account/subject/audience/generation are claims re-checked against the snapshot or the signed resource (BAS mantle.rs:168-172,247); account is checked only through resource/signature coverage. Revocation freshness is the snapshot window and the rollback guard is per-process (F13).

invariants.name: I5 A denied request sends no frame, leaks nothing, redeems no ticket, reads no store path, evaluates no goal
invariants.evidence: Remote receiver (the only production-wired site): no frame (remote_build.rs:13293 before 13296), constant string for every reason (attenuated_admission.rs:30; remote_build.rs:13591-13594), ticket unchanged (tests:288-293,583-587). Caveats: a nonce can be burned by a denial after verify (attenuated_admission.rs:217) and malformed presentations fail earlier with a serde message (remote_build.rs:8701). Store: out-of-view reads fail with a constant message before any lookup (restricted_view.rs:46-76) but `store info` opens the store first (store_cmd.rs:187). Project site: no production caller, so denial-before-evaluation is only function-level.

invariants.name: I6 Legacy bearer tickets keep working unchanged and are never described as delegated
invariants.evidence: Absent presentation returns Ok(()) before any new check (remote_build.rs:13588-13590); the field is skip_serializing_if/default so legacy frames are byte-identical (357-359); ticket create prints delegation 'legacy-bearer-not-delegated' with zero caveats (remote_build.rs:14554; authority_caveats.rs:182-195; tests/remote_credentials_cli.rs:77-80); test tests:300-322 admits bearer-only requests with and without a verifier.

invariants.name: I7 A broad store list under a restricted view is denied BEFORE scanning
invariants.evidence: deny_unrestricted_command_under_view (store_cmd.rs:165-177) runs first in cmd_store_async (180) and denies every action except Info, including future variants, before open_store; test restricted_view_denies_broad_listing_before_opening_the_store (store_cmd.rs ~2776-2795) proves List and Roots fail with the view denial instead of the open error. Dormant in production: cmd_store hard-codes view: None (store_cmd.rs:138).

invariants.name: I8 A project grant lowers declared to goal and rejects mismatched owner, nested goal, or another project's namespace
invariants.evidence: Owner mismatch and cross-namespace rewrites are rejected (authority.rs:130-144,242-267,299-303), but nested goals are admitted: project_value uses `suffix.split('/').all(project_segment)` (authority.rs:137-143), contradicting design.md 'nested goal rejected'. Pre-existing code, unchanged by this diff; resolve_project_target_with_authority has no production caller.

invariants.name: I9 Each issued grant reports its effective caveat chain
invariants.evidence: Mantle code issues no UCAN grants. The only 'issued' artefact is the legacy ticket, which prints a constant empty chain (remote_build.rs:14554). For presentations the chain is logged locally on admission (13597). GatewayVerifier::effective_caveat_chain (authority.rs:358-372) has no production caller besides remote admission, so gateway/project sessions report nothing outside tests. Cannot verify the stated intent (issuer-side report) because no issuance path exists.

questions.answer: WT=/home/brittonr/.cargo-target/agents-20261030/attenuation/worktree. Every denial that reaches the grant check yields the same Err(String) 'remote-attenuated-grant-denied' (WT/src/remote_build/attenuated_admission.rs:30). admit_attenuated_presentation_before_redemption maps every failure through `.map_err(|_| denied())` (WT/src/remote_build.rs:13591-13594) and the error type is Basalt's unit `Denied` (BAS/src/mantle.rs), so the cause is not even available to log. Collapsed causes: no AttenuationAdmission (13592); no verifier or snapshot (attenuated_admission.rs:190); bounds or project-scope mismatch (191); bind_remote_job failure (194); bad signature bytes (195); any GatewayVerifier::verify failure (207-215) - snapshot unreadable/invalid/expired (authority.rs:170-191), revoked or unknown proof/key, expired or not-yet-valid token (authority.rs:287,292), subject != token audience (mantle.rs:247), endpoint/audience/generation mismatch (mantle.rs:168-172), unknown/malformed/ordinal-gapped/over-bound caveat or parent-widening (authority_caveats.rs:48-66), replay duplicate or ledger error; effective_caveat_chain failure after verify (217). Wire: no frame - commit(...)? at remote_build.rs:13293 precedes the first write (13296) and runtime construction (13297); the CLI then prints 'remote production stdio serve once: remote-attenuated-grant-denied' (14254) with one exit code; the serve test asserts writer empty and error == the constant (tests:583-585). Logs: nothing on denial; only the success line (13597). Remaining differences, none an oracle for job id, path, caveat or reason: (1) a structurally malformed presentation (missing/unknown/mistyped field; deny_unknown_fields at attenuated_admission.rs:46) fails frame decoding before the bearer check with 'remote-frame-json-invalid: <serde message>' (remote_build.rs:8701, read at 13331) - sender data and schema names only, plus a version fingerprint; (2) state: ticket state cannot change (redemption mutates only uses_remaining, remote_build.rs:4713-4720), but the replay ledger is written when grant verification succeeds (holder_invocation.rs:835) so a denial at attenuated_admission.rs:217 or a later redemption failure leaves a burned nonce, and the first replay-stage reach creates the ledger lock/state files; no test snapshots the ledger; (3) timing: stages differ in cost (pre-I/O bounds checks; snapshot read+parse; several UCAN chain verifications; ledger read for duplicates; fsync'd write for admits), so coarse reason classes are timing-distinguishable and no constant-time claim exists; (4) pre-grant errors (unknown-remote-ticket-<id>, bearer, request validation, lock-timeout) are verbose but independent of the grant, and the grant is only evaluated after a valid bearer (13545), so unauthenticated peers learn nothing about grants.

Order confirmed in WT/src/remote_build.rs: lock 13526 -> load state 13534 -> receiver clock 13539 -> bearer verify_credentials 13545-13557 -> validate_concrete_request 13558 -> attenuation check 13559 -> redeem_and_commit_ticket_state 13561 (persist at 13568). Replay: the nonce is committed inside verifier.verify (attenuated_admission.rs:207) as the last step of verify_holder_signed_invocation, after token, holder-signature, profile and caveat-policy checks (BAS vendor/ucan/src/token/holder_invocation.rs:760-768,813,835; 'No work occurs after replay accepts'). So the record is written on grant verification success, not on request admission: a failure of effective_caveat_chain (attenuated_admission.rs:217) or of ticket persistence (13561-13570) leaves a consumed nonce and no redemption (fail-closed, nonce burned). Atomicity/durability: compare_and_swap under an exclusive flock with version check (replay.rs:194-225), temp file + fsync + rename + directory fsync (138-176), and classify_replay_commit requires Synchronized (BAS vendor/ucan/src/durable_authority.rs ~340-355); if rename succeeds and the directory fsync fails the record persists while an error is returned. Concurrency: the same presentation cannot be admitted twice - tickets.lock flock (remote_credential_state.rs:66-95, 5 s wait) serialises admissions across processes and the ledger CAS yields 1 Applied/7 Stale (pre-existing 8-thread test in replay.rs tests); there is no remote-level concurrency test. Two different presentations (distinct nonces) for the same job both admit, each spending a ticket use. If the replay write fails after the caveats pass: HolderInvocationReplayError::Backend -> Denied -> the constant denial, no redemption, no log; a full (8,192) or corrupt ledger denies permanently and silently (F3).

The BLAKE3 digest (domain 'mantle/remote/attenuated-build-request/v1' + length-framed fields, attenuated_admission.rs:129-156) covers: endpoint_id (receiver binding name), store_prefix, request_id, production_attempt.job_id, the target string (which embeds request_id and payload kind), payload id (drv_path/action_id), blake3 of the payload body, input_refs, source_input_refs, upload_bytes, build_time_limit_secs, and each expected output name and logical_path. It does NOT cover contains_raw_frontend_eval (rejected earlier if true), production_attempt.attempt_id and fence_generation, transfer_policy, resource_requirements, locality_scope, failure_debug_policy, failure_replay, endpoint_binding beyond its name, or the ticket id (remote_build.rs:403-430) - so docs:139 'any field' and the doc comment are false (F5). What the signatures commit to: BAS mantle.rs:168-215 builds the resource 'mantle://gateway/v1/' + length-framed hex of subject, account, project, endpoint, audience, policy_ref, target, then generation and the digest hex. The issuer's capability need only be a byte PREFIX of that string (UCAN containment is starts_with: vendor/ucan/src/verified.rs:594-598, verified-logic scope.rs covers); the test fixture signs the exact resource (tests:143-170) but the receiver does not require a minimum prefix. The holder signature always covers the exact resource, the ability, the token reference and the nonce (holder_invocation.rs:768-814), and the receiver recomputes the digest from the validated request. Hence: a presentation signed for request A cannot be admitted for a request that differs in any covered field (job, target/class, endpoint, upload bound, limits, payload, inputs, outputs, store prefix, generation, project) - the token's resource and the holder signature fail, and an exact-resource issuer grant fails even earlier; only the holder key can re-sign for a different request (fresh nonce), within the issuer's prefix and caveats. Uncovered fields can be changed after signing, and a presentation is not tied to a ticket.

Yes, with two notes. Clock: the host wall clock via ProductionClockPort (remote_build.rs:13479-13487; host_environment.rs:99-118) is read once under the lock (13539) and used for ticket authorisation and the grant (13545-13559; attenuated_admission.rs:207-215); the sender's now_unix_s and client_endpoint are explicitly ignored (remote_build.rs:352-356) and the forged-clock test passes u64::MAX (tests:493-516). Expiry/not-before: snapshot window `now < issued || now >= expires` (authority.rs:177-178); UCAN verification with VerificationLimits::strict() = zero skew (authority.rs:287,480; BAS vendor/ucan/src/token.rs:1664-1673) so nbf <= now <= exp, plus Mantle's half-open `now >= expires_at -> deny` (authority.rs:292) and Basalt's effective expiry (mantle.rs:264-267); parents are checked with the same time and the child window must be inside its proofs (token.rs verify_temporal_attenuation). u64 arithmetic: new Mantle code only compares; UCAN uses saturating adds (verified-logic ucan_token.rs:69-80). Revocation/roots/keys/proofs/policy come only from the operator snapshot, re-read per call (authority.rs:170-217) and checked on every chain verification (CurrentRevocations, authority.rs ~485-505; check_roots mantle.rs:348); endpoint id and project scope come from the operator EndpointBinding admitted by endpoint_config.rs:114-130 (remote_build.rs:13421-13425); the site policy is `value == exact` from the validated request (authority.rs:297-303). Notes: (a) account is the one sender-supplied field never compared to a receiver fact (only via resource/signature coverage); (b) revocation freshness is simply the snapshot window and the in-memory rollback guard is useless for stdio-once processes (F13); the ticket deadline and the grant's signed expiry are both compared with the same server time.

Closed for presented grants everywhere; the start-time check is narrower than documented. Absent snapshot: open_operator_authority returns Ok(None) (attenuated_admission.rs:228-229); a presented grant is then refused (190; remote_build.rs:13592) while bearer-only traffic is unchanged; a file created later is ignored until restart. Invalid CONTENT (malformed JSON, wrong version, expired window, policy-hash mismatch, bad keys/proofs/roots): remote serve STARTS, because GatewayVerifier::open only calls private_read plus the ledger directory check (authority.rs:160-168); each presentation is then denied in load() (170-191). So 'a present but invalid snapshot stops remote serve' (docs:141, doc comment at attenuated_admission.rs:223-225) is true only for the cases below and untested. Start fails (RunError 'remote-attenuation-authority-invalid', attenuated_admission.rs:230,238, called at remote_build.rs:14236 before any request is read) for: stat error other than NotFound; unreadable file; symlink (symlink_metadata passes, private_read opens with O_NOFOLLOW, authority.rs:543-546, so even a valid target or dangling link fails); non-regular file; owner != process uid; mode & 0o077 != 0; > 1 MiB (MAX_AUTHORITY_BYTES plus take(MAX+1)); missing, symlinked, non-0700 or wrong-owner replay directory (replay.rs:250-259). The parent state dir's permissions are not checked (other users with write access could delete/rename the files - DoS, not forgery, because ownership is checked). A FIFO would block open (operator-only). The fixture executor loads the snapshot but never enforces it (F7), and --executor defaults to fixture (main.rs:2801).

Yes - for the intended delegation model this defeats the purpose of T3.1. Admission always requires the ticket bearer (remote_build.rs:13545) and the presentation is optional (13588-13590); no 'requires grant' property exists (remote_credentials.rs:447-457) and the design mandates it (design.md:71-72). Any recipient who can be admitted therefore holds the unrestricted bearer and can omit the presentation; the restriction only affects parties who volunteer it, which is the 'unsigned sidecar bypassable by the parent bearer' that ADR 0090:9,66-67 rejects. A holder without the bearer cannot use the grant at all. Documentation: docs/remote-credentials.md:143 states the mechanism accurately but understates it (it suggests a class of 'holders who also hold the bearer' versus others; there is none) and the headline text at :137 says the grant 'restrict[s] one job'; the status record (grant-sites-status-2026-10-30.md:18) and the spec scenario 'Restricted grant refuses a second job' say nothing about the bypass, and tasks T3.1 should not be ticked. Additional undocumented limits: holder attenuation is operator-gated (F4), 'job' is a label (F2), grants are ignored by non-enforcing paths (F7). Meaningful remaining value: voluntary least-privilege and an audit record. Fix: an enforcing mode (provisioned authority => presentation required, or a per-ticket flag) or bearer-less grant admission.

Gating precedes every read in the restricted type: RestrictedOutputLookup::find, find_with_layer and find_remote call self.admit(path)? as their first statement (crates/crunch-store/src/restricted_view.rs:57-76); admit rebuilds the canonical logical path with to_absolute_path_with_prefix, rejects > 512 bytes, then asks the view (46-55); there is no Deref/into_inner, and resolve_ca_mapping/overlay_report are not exposed on the wrapper. A refusal is the constant 'store: restricted-store-view-denied' and does not depend on existence (tests assert both for present and absent paths). Shell: deny_unrestricted_command_under_view (store_cmd.rs:165-177) runs first (180) and denies everything except Info, including future variants, before the store opens; List/Roots are proven denied before open (store_cmd.rs tests ~2776-2795). For Info the path is parsed and gated only after open_store (187 -> 788); admitted PathInfo prints references/deriver/node unredacted (F8). Path confusion: the user string is parsed by StorePath::from_absolute_path_with_prefix (vendor/nix-compat store_path/mod.rs:170-176 -> from_bytes -> validate_name, charset a-zA-Z0-9 + - _ ? = . only, vendor/nix-compat store_path/mod.rs:292-293,307) and the view sees only the canonical re-rendering `{store_dir}/{digest}-{name}`, so '..', '.', repeated or trailing slashes, percent-encoding, non-ASCII and alternate digest spellings are rejected or normalised before the view; case is significant; the view sees the hash-bearing store path, so name-only patterns cannot be expressed (safe but over-restrictive); a symlink node is only displayed, never followed. The tests cover an in-view hit, an out-of-view existing path, a fragment, '/mantle/store/../etc' and a digest look-alike; trailing slash/percent/case are not exercised and no test proves the inner service is not consulted. A view that 'cannot be evaluated': LogicalPathView::admits returns bool (no error channel), so unparsable or oversized input is deny; implementor panics abort the read. Production: cmd_store passes view: None (store_cmd.rs:138) and no LogicalPathView implementation exists outside tests, so the control is dormant (F8).

Confirmed. Unknown type: PatternPolicies::policy_for returns a policy only for (mantle, filter-v1) (authority_caveats.rs:48-51) so any other caveat identity is denied by UCAN (BAS vendor/ucan/src/token.rs:2642-2651); with_decoded_chain returns None for a foreign domain/type, empty or > 8192-byte payload, non-JSON, duplicate or unknown fields (deny_unknown_fields; escaped strings fail the borrowed &str decode) and > 8 alternatives (authority_caveats.rs:81-104); an unknown kind is Filter::DenyAll (caveat.rs:226); malformed known kinds are errors (225). Chain bound: caveats.len() > MAX_CHAIN -> None (authority_caveats.rs:82-84), from_records re-checks length and exact ordinals 00..07 (caveat.rs:290-310), attenuate caps at 8, and the report path stops before parsing an over-bound chain (authority_caveats.rs:200-209). Order cannot widen: newest-first application (caveat.rs:325-330) plus the per-prefix original-input check with the site policy (338-355); UCAN's preservation is order-insensitive set containment (verified.rs:1058-1070), so gaps, duplicates and reorders are caught only by the ordinal check, which denies. Panics/allocation: no unwrap/expect/panic in the new production code of attenuated_admission.rs, restricted_view.rs or authority_caveats.rs (only debug_assert!); indexing is bounded (segments <= 16, `self.caveats[..end]` with end <= len); JSON parsing is limited to <= 8 payloads of <= 8192 bytes with serde_json's recursion limit, so allocation is bounded and there is no recursion beyond that. EffectiveCaveatChain::from_documents never parses beyond the bound and copies patterns only for chains that passed Caveat::from_wire (authority_caveats.rs:244-300).

Confirmed on both points. Nested goals: project_value admits any '/'-separated suffix whose segments pass project_segment (WT/src/nix_gateway/authority.rs:130-144), and the fixture's rewrite targets /project/project-a/goal/packages/check (authority/tests.rs ~520), contradicting design.md's 'nested goal rejected'. resolve_project_target_with_authority (WT/src/project_build/authority.rs:101-106) is called only from tests; the module has #![allow(dead_code)] (line 3) and verify_project_declaration is #[allow(dead_code)] (authority.rs:241). Risk: low and latent - owner prefix is enforced on the original and every rewritten output (authority.rs:299-303; verify_project_declaration 242-267), '.'/'..' and empty segments are rejected, so a nested suffix stays inside /project/<owner>/; real selectors are segment lists (ProjectTarget::Attribute), so the design text rather than the code looks wrong. Did the chain-report change make anything worse? It adds no authorization dependency and no new input; effective_caveat_chain (authority.rs:358-372) is a read-only projection, but (a) it calls load() again, which re-reads the snapshot and updates the in-memory observed state, (b) it checks expiry but not revocation, so 'only while live' means 'unexpired', (c) in the remote path a failure there happens after the replay nonce was burned (attenuated_admission.rs:217), and (d) from_documents labels a zero-caveat chain 'holder-attenuated-ucan'. For gateway/project sessions it has no production caller, so the T3.4 claim is overstated.

The report is emitted only (a) at `ticket create`, as a constant legacy chain on stdout to the operator (remote_build.rs:14554), and (b) as a local tracing::info! after an ADMITTED presentation (remote_build.rs:13597), never on the wire and never on denial. The sink is the process's tracing subscriber, stderr (main.rs:3640-3643), active only with --verbose, --log-level or RUST_LOG (default WARN; machine-readable output suppresses logging unless requested, mantle-application-contract output_format.rs:51-54). Under SSH-stdio the remote stderr returns to the client, i.e. to the presenting holder, who already has every caveat because a child token must embed all parent caveats verbatim; a bearer-only party cannot trigger the log because it requires a verified holder signature. The report is redacted for secrets (no token, signature or denied-request detail; unaccepted caveats expose only a payload digest) but accepted patterns and templates, which can name job ids or project goals, are printed in full. GatewayVerifier::effective_caveat_chain requires a live, non-cloneable GatewaySession (authority.rs:358-372) and has no other production caller. Residual exposure is to whoever can read the receiver's logs (operators, a shared journal). The log line precedes the redemption commit (F9).

Unknown caveat - real boundary yes: loop case 'unknown-caveat' (tests:422) and the serve-path test (535-587, writer empty, constant error) with ticket uses unchanged; only the unknown-kind form (not unregistered domain/type). Chain over bound - real boundary yes: 9 caveats refused (loop) and 8 admitted (tests:519-533). Caveat on 'unchanged state': assert_refused_without_effect captures `before` after the call (line 289), so its state-equality assertion is vacuous for the 11 loop cases and only `uses_remaining == TICKET_USES` is real (it is the only field redemption mutates); the status record's 'state byte-equal' is overstated. Also unexercised: not-yet-valid token, wrong endpoint/generation/audience/holder key/signature, parent-caveat drop/modify/duplicate/reorder, revoked parent, concurrency, ledger full/failure, invalid snapshot at start, fixture path (F11).
